questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good opportunities for learning Russian. The opportunity to (academically) learn more about a country/culture, which I had little previous knowlegde about.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found the host university's course system rather confusing, which was made worse by the fact that there were being made changes to the system, when I arrived. This made it difficult to find a course combination, which could actually work. Contact information was reasonably accessible.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I (and some of the others travelling from Denmark) spoke with department and exchange coordinators and attended an Erasmus intro meeting.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I initially found accomodation through the host university. However, early on I found an appartment (on Stabu Iela) with some of the other students from Denmark. We found this accomodation through other Erasmus students. Reznas student accomodation was ok, but for sanitary reasons I strongly recommend that students avoid Prima hostel (which was also an option provided by the host university). I would advise students to search for other options in the city, rather than simply going with the options provided by the host university.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The appartment I ended up living in for most of the semester was more central (to both the city center and most faculties) than the student accomodations, so I don't really have an on-campus experience to compare with.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The price of the appartment was very reasonable and provided in every sense more value for the money.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The course system was confusing. Many courses were, which were applied for in the spring, were no longer available. Other courses, which had been approved over the summer, had conflicting schedules. This meant that I (and the other students from Denmark) basically had to start from the beginning. This was very frustrating, because our OLA's had to be changed multiple times in the spring, before they were approved, which no seems wholly meaningless.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Many courses were, which were applied for in the spring, were no longer available. Other courses, which had been approved over the summer, had conflicting schedules. Some course schedules were also changed/decided in the first lessons. This meant that I (and the other students from Denmark) basically had to start from the beginning. This was very frustrating, because our OLA's had to be changed multiple times in the spring, before they were approved, which no seems wholly meaningless.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Department coordinators, who responded very quickly during the registration weeks.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Many courses were not an option. Also, the process was so frustrating that at the end, it was more important (to me) that the registration got done, than which courses I would have.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Spend as little time as possible on the OLA in the spring. It is almost completely useless. Look at some courses over the summer, but don't put in too much effort, before you arrive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level of the courses was very low. Compared to Danish standards it was like gymnasiet/(high school). The exception was the Russian courses, which had very good quality. I would also not that some educators had very bad communication. Deadlines and exam info was severely lacking despite numerous requests and sometimes only communicated a week before the deadline. Lastly, I must note that one educator lowered grades for some of the students, who handed in papers for the re-hand-in deadline, which is not academically responsible.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level of the courses was very low. Compared to Danish standards it was like gymnasiet/(high school). The exception was the Russian courses, which had very good quality.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were different teaching styles in the Russian courses, but I would rank both on the same level as UCPH. However, the other courses did not compare to UCPH in terms of academic level, and often seemed like opinion and basic knowlegde rather than the product of academic study.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Russian as Foreign 3rd level (B1) Part 1
Russian as foreign language (Level A2 1)
Media Representation, Ethics, Memory and the Holocaust
Historical Narratives in Propaganda: Cases studies of Russia and Ukraine
Environment and Sustainable Development in the Baltic Sea Region
International Media Law
A History of Latvian Culture: 20th Century

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Russian as Foreign 3rd level (B1) Part 1 (good quality teaching)
Russian as foreign language (Level A2 1) (good quality teaching (especially for getting grammar into your spoken language))

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many and varied Erasmus opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would simply say that there was something for everyone.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would suggest participating in speed-friending or similar events, because being part of one or more groups of Erasmus students will be very good for having further non-academic experiences during the exchange.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The are museums, cinemas, cultural events, other nearby towns, relatively nearby beaches if the weather allows for it, Tallinn and Vilnius are also possible weekend destinations.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was ok. There are some cultural differences in terms of communication at the university (both regarding exams as mentioned above but also regarding the death of one of our educators during the semester, which has never been officially communicated).

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mainly ended up socialising with Erasmus students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There are some cultural differences in terms of communication at the university (both regarding exams as mentioned above but also regarding the death of one of our educators during the semester, which has never been officially communicated).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I particularly enjoyed the culinary experiences, the nature, and some museums.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't spend a lot of time on the courses for the OLA, before registration week.
Avoid Prima for accomodation (find something different in stead to begin with, and consider looking for an appartment with other students in the city after registration week).
Focus on the cultural and social opportunities, while you are abroad.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The cultural and social experiences.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Communication regarding exams.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
